source_repair.public_task_text:
Implement solve(intervals). intervals contains 0..4 closed intervals [lo,hi] with integer endpoints -3<=lo<=hi<=3. Return a list of lists representing the union as sorted disjoint closed intervals. Merge overlapping intervals and intervals touching at the same endpoint; [0,0] and [1,1] do NOT touch. Return [] for empty input.
Public examples: [{"args": [[]], "expected": []}, {"args": [[[-3, 1], [-1, 0]]], "expected": [[-3, 1]]}, {"args": [[[-2, 2], [0, 2]]], "expected": [[-2, 2]]}, {"args": [[[1, 1], [0, 0]]], "expected": [[0, 0], [1, 1]]}]
source_repair.interpretation: Actual answer repair changed only the adjacency comparison. This is not itself Skill evolution or a No-Skill versus Skill causal improvement.

procedure: When implementing a union/merge of closed intervals, merge the next interval into the current output interval only when its lo is <= the current interval's hi.
Do not widen the merge condition to lo <= hi + 1 (adjacent integers) unless the contract explicitly states that adjacent-but-disjoint intervals merge.

Before finalizing, locate any contract sentence or public example that distinguishes touching at the same endpoint from adjacency (e.g. two single-point intervals one unit apart) and confirm the merge condition reproduces it.
If the contract's touching definition is ambiguous and no distinguishing example exists, keep the literal endpoint condition and note the ambiguity rather than guessing a wider merge.
rules.when: A public task obligation asks to merge closed intervals into a union of sorted disjoint intervals, with a stated rule about which intervals touch or merge.
exceptions: Contracts that explicitly define adjacent integer endpoints as touching or merging require the opposite comparison; no such condition-reversal case is present in the supplied evidence, so this exception is untested.

skill_proposal.edit_reason: ev_d0c012bb737f1532397d6d77 shows a draft failing public checks with merge condition lo <= out[-1][1] + 1 while the contract says [0,0] and [1,1] do NOT touch; the revised implementation using lo <= out[-1][1] passed the same public check, giving an observed failure and a supplied successful alternative for this exact mechanism. No reversal case (a contract requiring adjacent merging) was supplied, so the exception boundary is stated but untested; no causal No-Skill/Current effect is claimed since both arms share the trajectory.
limitations: The source supports the endpoint comparison, not the universal ambiguity default.
The machine scope only requires requested_behavior; textual when is not an implemented routing filter.
No reverse-policy example was supplied to this update; the stated exception was a proposal, not a validated boundary.

reverse_policy_execution.interpretation: Both No-Skill and the raw frozen candidate pass all shown h0 positions. The candidate follows the new adjacent-integer policy here; no positive gain or proven rule-following is established.
